# Camber Reign

> Camber Reign is a free, single-player 3D browser racing game by AppsOverFlow. Race seven computer-controlled rivals across thirty-four asphalt circuits in one of 33 cars, earn race credits, and upgrade your car. No account, no install, no purchases.

## About the game

Camber Reign runs directly in a modern web browser (WebGL 2 required) at https://camber-reign.web.app/. A single human player races seven computer-controlled opponents — Mira, Jax, Nova, Ren, Kai, Aria and Leo — in an eight-car field over three laps. Gameplay centres on drifting for score, a rechargeable nitro boost, and earning race credits to install permanent, per-car upgrades. Progress is saved locally in the browser; there is no online multiplayer and no real-money payment.

## How to play

- Choose Cars in Race HQ, preview a car and select Open garage. Use Upgrades to spend earned credits on performance, or Paint for free colours and finishes.
- Choose Circuits, preview one of thirty-four routes and select that circuit to return to Race HQ. Choose Circuit race, Time attack or Three-race tour, then Race Now to start.
- Acceleration is automatic. Hold the left or right side of the steering thumbpad, or drag it for fine control; release to center. You can also drag across the race view or use Left/Right or A/D on a keyboard. On a compatible phone, open Pause → Steering → Enable tilt, allow motion access if asked, and use Recenter tilt in your comfortable holding position. Touch steering always overrides tilt, and unavailable or stale sensor data falls back to touch. Turn sharply at speed to drift automatically. Hold Nitro or Shift to boost; release to recharge. Nitro is the only on-screen pedal. Down/S is an optional keyboard brake and Space holds the optional handbrake.
- Ease the steering back into line after an automatic drift to bank clean drift points; Space is an optional keyboard handbrake.
- Hold Shift (or the Nitro button) for a boost on clear straights; release to recharge.
- Complete three laps through the ordered checkpoints to finish and earn credits.
- Touch controls and landscape orientation are supported on phones. Optional tilt requires a compatible motion sensor and permission when requested.
- Light barrier scrapes preserve most forward momentum. A hard impact briefly reduces drive and interrupts nitro, and loses any unbanked drift points. If you remain pressed into a barrier while accelerating for about 2.4 seconds, the player car automatically returns to a clear point behind its last valid progress. A car far off the road recovers after about 0.9 seconds while acceleration is requested. Recovery may wait for a clear gap, rewinds any crossed checkpoint requirement and has a three-second cooldown. Holding the brake or handbrake does not trigger automatic recovery. R or Reset car remains available for a manual return to the last valid road position. Neither method grants lap progress or refills nitro; race time keeps running.

## Circuits

The 34-course collection combines nine original Camber Reign circuits, compact adaptations of all 23 venues on the official 2026 calendar checked on 1 October 2026, and Sakhir and Jeddah as original-calendar bonuses. Playable arcade laps are shorter than the real venues, with widened turns and flattened elevation. Suzuka is explicitly unrolled into a non-crossing course; its real overpass is not reproduced.

- Harbor Flow — about 1.22 km per lap; beginner-friendly waterfront sweepers.
- Dockyard Technical — about 1.53 km; a tight sequence of dockside turns.
- Coast Run — about 1.13 km; open coastal curves for sustained acceleration.
- Summit Switchback — about 1.66 km; technical pine-lined switchbacks.
- Bay Grand Prix — about 1.53 km; a wide permanent circuit with flowing chicanes.
- Breakwater Run — about 2.09 km; A long sea-wall straight, sweeping headlands and an inland S-bend beside basalt outcrops and a working lighthouse.
- Copper Canyon — about 2.36 km; Carry speed between sandstone mesas, then brake for a broad canyon hairpin and a linked pair of technical turns.
- Cedar Ridge — about 2.41 km; Find a rhythm through cedar-lined bends, open the throttle on the forest straight, and sweep past timber lodges under the ridgeline.
- Neon Freight — about 2.26 km; A floodlit freight district with a long loading-yard straight, generous ninety-degree turns and a fast return past container stacks.

Current-calendar adaptations: Albert Park, Shanghai, Suzuka, Miami, Gilles Villeneuve, Monaco, Barcelona-Catalunya, Red Bull Ring, Silverstone, Spa-Francorchamps, Hungaroring, Zandvoort, Monza, Madring, Baku City, Sepang, Marina Bay, Circuit of the Americas, Hermanos Rodríguez, Interlagos, Las Vegas Strip, Lusail, Yas Marina.
Original-calendar bonus adaptations: Bahrain International, Jeddah Corniche.
Venue outline data: Tomislav Bacinger / f1-circuits, MIT, with compact arcade modifications. Sources and notices: https://camber-reign.web.app/credits/#circuit-data

## Race cars

The garage contains 33 artist-made manufacturer models across 16 brands. All are available from the start and retain their actual model names, including labelled artist interpretations. Each car has five upgrade levels for Engine, Tyres, Nitro and Handling, purchased with earned race credits. Road cars, classics, grand tourers and track-focused models use arcade tuning rather than real-world performance specifications.

Search the collection by car, manufacturer or style. Accents, spaces and punctuation do not need to match exactly: “Huracan” finds Huracán and “GTR” finds GT-R. Filter by manufacturer or favourites, sort by latest arrivals, speed, handling or name, and use Clear filters to reset the view. Compare with your car shows top speed, acceleration, handling and Nitro differences, including each car’s saved upgrades.

After a valid lap, a short notice shows the last lap time and the next lap number. From the second completed lap, it compares that time with your previous best in the current race; the third lap is marked Final lap.

## Race modes and local progression

- Circuit race: one player and seven computer-controlled opponents over three laps. Club, Sport and Pro change rival pace; opponents still follow the same physical simulation and checkpoints.
- Time attack: solo three-lap runs, local personal bests and Bronze/Silver/Gold targets for the chosen car and course.
- Three-race tour: the same car and difficulty across three distinct circuits. Every valid finish earns its ordinary race credits, and the tour totals earned credits and position points.
- Medal targets describe this arcade game, not real-world motorsport records. Records are separate by car, circuit, mode and difficulty. Medals are saved in this browser when storage is available. Tours require working browser storage to carry the same car and earned rounds between circuits. An unfinished tour is replaced only after an explicit Start new tour choice.
- Circuit race and tour finish rewards: 900/650/500/350/300/250/200/150 credits for places 1–8. Solo time attack: 350 credits. Both add one credit per 20 drift points, up to a 500-credit bonus. Incomplete and over-15-minute runs do not award credits.

## Key Facts

- Publisher: AppsOverFlow (https://appsoverflow.web.app/).
- Free to play; no account, no install and no real-money purchases.
- Runs in a modern web browser; WebGL 2 and an internet connection are required to load.
- Single-player only: one human racer versus seven computer-controlled opponents (Mira, Jax, Nova, Ren, Kai, Aria and Leo) in an eight-car field over three laps.
- 33 cars: individually sourced manufacturer representations across 16 brands; 34 asphalt circuits, all available from the start.
- Each car has five upgrade levels for Engine, Tyres, Nitro and Handling, bought with earned race credits.
- Progress (records, credits, upgrades and paint) is saved locally in the browser; there is no online multiplayer.

## Real-car collection

Choose from 33 independently sourced manufacturer representations across 16 brands. Real cars include McLaren 570S Coupé, McLaren Senna, McLaren P1 GTR, Ferrari 458 Spider, Lamborghini Aventador, Koenigsegg One:1, Pagani Zonda C12, Bugatti Veyron, Maserati GranTurismo MC Stradale, Lotus Elise, Audi R8 Custom, Rimac Concept One, Porsche 911 (930) Turbo, GMA T.50 Custom, Aston Martin One-77, Rimac Nevera, Porsche 911 GT3, Lamborghini Gallardo 2004, Lamborghini Huracán, BMW i8, BMW F22 Eurofighter, Audi R8 LMS GT3, Audi R18, Ferrari 250 GTO, Ferrari Testarossa, Mercedes-AMG GT, Nissan GT-R 2018, McLaren 650S GT3, BMW M3 E46 Coupé, Audi Quattro Rally, Lamborghini Countach LP500S, Ferrari Enzo, Porsche 919 Hybrid. Each car has its own game tuning and saved upgrades. Speed, handling and Nitro ratings describe the arcade game, not manufacturer specifications. Paint changes are free on supported body materials.

New manufacturer models load only when selected; the catalogue uses lightweight rendered previews. Original model finishes and source credits are retained. The crowd uses individually posed animated 3D spectators with waves, claps, cheering and filming; it is not photoreal video.
